chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Giyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who marries with an immediate (dower) and a delayed (dower), he (peace be upon him) said: 'The delayed one is until death or separation'.
ai.seo_question: What is the default duration for a delayed dower in Shia Islamic marriage law?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of Ghayath ibn Ibrahim to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith establishes the default legal presumption for an unspecified delayed dower (mu'ajjal), ruling that it remains a debt until the marriage concludes via death or divorce. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining financial rights in the absence of explicit contractual terms, ensuring the wife's financial security is preserved until the marital bond is formally dissolved.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the man who married with an immediate (dower) and a delayed (dower). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The delayed one is until death or separation’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following:

“About the case of a man who marries a woman for a mahr (dower) payable immediately and a part of it on credit, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The due date for payment of what is on credit of mahr (dower) is on their separation or death.’”
